WORKSHEET · CLASS 24 · AGES 4 YEARS

Little Pizza Chef Worksheet for Age 4

Top the pizza like a real chef: 5 tomatoes, 5 mushrooms, 5 olives.

← Little Builder ChallengePrevious worksheetCounting Caterpillar →Next worksheet
ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

A pizza is the happiest counting board in the world. Topping it with exactly five of each ingredient turns draw-5 into a game with a delicious finish, and counting each topping as it lands builds one-to-one discipline: five means five, not six, however hungry the chef. Fifteen toppings all together is a proud big number made of three friendly fives.

  • Drawing a given number of items
  • Counting to 5 three times
  • Keeping count across three groups
  • Saying 5+5+5=15 with fingers

On the sheet: Draw 5 tomato slices, 5 mushrooms and 5 olive rings on the pizza.

HOW TO USE IT

Three easy steps.

  1. Count out loud together

    Touch each thing as you count it — finger on apple, circle on caterpillar. Touching keeps the count honest.

  2. Write big

    The answer boxes are big on purpose. Big wobbly numerals are exactly what they should be at four.

  3. Check by counting again

    Counting a second time (and getting the same number!) is the skill. Celebrate the recount, not just the answer.

TEACHING TIPS

Little things that help.

Use real things first

Count spoons, steps and apples in the kitchen before the pencil comes out. Numbers live in the world first.

Mistakes are data

If the count comes out different each time, slow down and count as a team. That is the whole lesson.

Keep sessions tiny

One sheet, maybe two rows of it, is plenty for a four-year-old’s counting stamina.

Answer guide

Each topping appears exactly 5 times — 15 pieces of pizza art in all.

WHERE THIS FITS

The class behind it.

This worksheet belongs to Counting & Number Recognition (Class 24) on the Age 4 learning path, and the whole maths collection lives at /worksheets/maths/. One finished sheet is a full session — download it, print it, and let the fridge door be the gallery.
